topics.topic: Government Notifies Coking Coal as Critical & Strategic Mineral under MMDR Act, 1957
topics.why_in_news: Union Government notified coking coal as a Critical and Strategic Mineral under the MMDR Act, 1957 to strengthen steel-sector security and reduce import vulnerability.
prelims_quick_notes: Coking coal essential for blast-furnace steelmaking.
Produces coke when heated in absence of air.
Coke acts as fuel and reducing agent in steel production.
India highly dependent on imported coking coal.
Critical mineral classification enables regulatory relaxations.
Move linked with National Steel Policy goals.
Strategic minerals important for economic and industrial security.
important_facts: MMDR Act stands for Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957.
Coking coal included as Critical and Strategic Mineral under First Schedule.
India possesses significant coking coal resources mainly in Jharkhand.
Nearly 95% of steel-sector coking coal demand met through imports.
Coking coal differs from thermal coal.
Anthracite has highest carbon content among coal types.
Bituminous coal commonly used for metallurgical purposes.
Steel sector heavily dependent on coking coal availability.
key_highlights: Regulatory approvals expected to become faster.
Public consultation requirements relaxed for critical mineral projects.
Supply-chain resilience for steel sector prioritised.
Policy shift towards strategic-mineral governance highlighted.
exam_relevance: Important for Geography, Economy and Mineral Resources.
Useful for energy security and industrial policy topics.
Can be linked with steel industry and critical minerals.
prelims_traps: Coking coal differs from thermal coal.
Coke produced by heating coal without air.
Critical minerals linked with strategic and industrial security.
